text: In Hamiltonian mechanics the time evolution of a phase-space function f with no explicit time dependence is given by the Poisson bracket df/dt = {f, ___}; consequently f is conserved when this bracket vanishes.
explanation: The book writes df/dt = {f, H} + ∂f/∂t, so with no explicit time dependence df/dt = {f, H}, and f is conserved iff {f, H} = 0. Under Dirac's canonical quantization this Poisson bracket becomes the commutator (1/iℏ)[f̂, Ĥ].
